title: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isIso_baseChange_of_smooth
statement: Let f:X→Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let g:Y′→Y be smooth. Given a cartesian square with upper map g′:X′→X and left map f′:X′→Y′, and K in the bounded below derived category of abelian sheaves on X_ét whose homology has torsion orders invertible on Y (Etale.DerivedCategory.Plus.orderInvertibleOnHomology f K), the component at K of the derived étale base-change natural transformation Lg^* Rf_* → Rf′_* Lg′^* is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the set of primes whose images are units in $\Gamma(Y,\top)$. Unfolding $hK$ and the geometric-stalk definitions, for every cohomology degree and geometric stalk element $x$, the integer $n=\operatorname{addOrderOf}(x)$ maps to a unit in $\Gamma(Y,\top)$. If $n>0$, each prime divisor $p$ of $n$ also maps to a unit: writing $n=pr$ and choosing an inverse of $n$, the product $r n^{-1}$ is an inverse of $p$. Thus each stalk element is killed by an integer whose prime divisors lie in $\mathcal P$. If $n=0$ and a geometric point existed, the ring map $\Gamma(Y,\top)\to\Omega$ induced by the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ would send the unit $0\in\Gamma(Y,\top)$ to zero, impossible; hence this case has no stalks. Therefore $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(X_{\Et})$ by [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion].

proof.text: Apply [sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change] after relabelling its $(S,T,X,Y;f,g,h,e)$ as $(Y,X,Y\prime,X\prime;g,f,f\prime,g\prime)$ in the given cartesian square. Its smooth morphism is therefore the present $g$, its quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism is the present $f$, and its input is the present $K$; Step 1 supplies the required allowable-torsion hypothesis. The resulting isomorphism is the component of the derived base-change map with endpoints $Lg^*Rf_*K$ and $Rf\prime_*Lg\prime^*K$. The definition [sbc-def-base-change-map] identifies this morphism with [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] on the relabelled square. The latter gives the component explicitly as $\eta_{f',Lg^*Rf_*K}$ followed by $Rf'_*(\theta^D_{Rf_*K})$ followed by $Rf'_*Lg'^*(\varepsilon_{f,K})$, where $\theta^D:Lf'^*Lg^*\cong Lg'^*Lf^*$ is induced by $gf'=fg'$. Unfolding upstream MorphismDefs.lean, baseChangeUnitStep.app is exactly this unit, baseChangeSquareStep.hom.app is exactly this direct image of the composition comparison, and baseChangeCounitStep.app is exactly this direct image of the pulled-back counit. Its pullbackSquareComparison is $(L(gf')^*\cong Lf'^*Lg^*)^{-1}$ followed by the square equality and $L(fg')^*\cong Lg'^*Lf^*$, so it has the same orientation as $\theta^D$. Thus Etale.baseChange.app K is this very three-arrow composite, not merely a map with the same endpoints. The target component is consequently an isomorphism.
